newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- South Africa's neighbours in southern Africa, which are enjoying generous trade concessions as members of the Lome convention, could soon come under pressure to open their markets to the European Union when the trade and aid accord between the EU and its 70 African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) partners comes up for renewal in 2000.
- The money market shortage shot up to a record high of 11.126 billion rand last Friday before easing by nine million rand to 11.117 billion rand on Saturday, the Reserve Bank said on Monday.
- A KwaZulu-Natal black investment group, Nqubeko Investments, has tied up with Malaysian investment group Taipan Consolidated Projects to form a joint venture company.

- Drive drunk and spend the beginning of the new year behind bars -- that was the warning from South African traffic authorities who have threatened roadblocks trhoughout Johannesburg to nab drunken drivers and revellers who are behaving badly.
